log.migrated.description: The engine of the process applied a migration definition to the file, from its format number to this one (docs/spec/installation.md#stored-data-migration).

log.open.description: The first line of every event file.

log.closed.description: The host process is ending. cause is signal for the first termination signal before quit, exit-request for a request to end the process, and exit for the end of the process; signal is the number of the termination signal when cause is signal. The writer stores it through its own path, so it passes every gate.

log.dropped.description: A range of seq that the writer refused; it explains the gap. channel is other for the events of the levels error, warn and info and debug for the events of the levels debug and trace; it is stored in the main file. queued is the largest number of events that waited in the writer queue at a refusal that the record counts; it is absent for a loss that a source reports through the pull.

log.policy.description: The policy of the event log that is now in force: source is default when no policy file exists and file when the policy file holds it; classes holds the least severe level that is stored for each class. The first policy of a writer and every change of it are stored; the same policy again is not.

log.pruned.description: The retention removed the files of the oldest runs because the files of the runs passed the bound: files and bytes are what it removed, runs are the names of the runs (`<role>-<boot>`), from_us and to_us are the range of the time of their events, remaining is the size of the files that are left and bound is the bound. The level is warn when remaining is still over bound because only the run of the writer and pinned runs are left.

log.gated.description: The number of events of the class and the level that the gate of the host refused since the earlier report, so no event is lost without a count.

log.rotated.description: A file was closed as the generation with this number and a new file started; no generation is removed.

native.record.<level>.description: A record of the native library.

page.record.<level>.description: A record of the page, including the errors that a person sees.

sidecar.record.<level>.description: A line that a sidecar wrote to its standard error, stored by the host with the name of the sidecar as the place.

sok.command.description: One run of the command line tool: the command word, the arguments and the error text cut to 1024 bytes (`truncated` is true when either was cut), the microseconds, the exit status, and the first line of its standard error for a status other than 0.

sok.replay.divergence.description: The first stored screen hash of a session that differs from the replayed hash: the segment (the boot of the run of the sidecar), the sequence, the layer of the stored hash (`sidecar` or `plugin`), the replayed hash (`none` for a page frame without a sidecar frame) and the stored hash.

sok.panic.description: A panic of the command line tool: the goroutine or thread that panicked (`main` for the command), the panic text and the stack at the panic.

sok.record.<level>.description: A record of the command line tool, such as a refused policy file of the place log policy.

page.console.<method>.description: What the page writes to its console; the text is cut to 8192 bytes while it is built and `truncated` is true when it was cut.

page.trace.<event>.description: The performance trace of the page, while it is on.

page.trace.declared-ui.snapshot.skipped.description: A value of a declared UI status was overwritten while its snapshot was in transit, while the performance trace is on: the main page writes it with the count of the overwritten values, which the snapshot message carries as its skipped field (docs/spec/plugin-processes.md, rule 2).

page.trace.modal.answer.description: An answer of the open native modal that the page receives, while the trace is on: key is the answered key, and the event is written at the receipt of the answer by the page, because the overlay document has no trace switch. A state report of the modal document is not an answer and writes no event.

page.trace.picker.close.description: The close of the native picker layer, while the trace is on: reason is the reason of the close, one of `replaced` (another layer opened), `settled` (the layout settled), `fullscreen` (a card entered or left fullscreen), `toggle` (its button closed it), `pick` (an item was picked), `dismiss` (core.modal.dismiss), and `command` (core.picker.close, which the page runs for Escape and for a press outside the layer).

host.call.timeout.description: A command that the exposure relay forwarded to a surface page got no reply within its declared time limit: plugin is the plugin of the surface and command is the forwarded method (docs/spec/exposure.md#errors).

host.trace.call.late-reply.description: A reply to a forwarded command arrived after its time limit, and the relay refused it: delay is the time in milliseconds from the send of the command to the reply (docs/spec/exposure.md#errors).

host.trace.exposure.request.description: The host sent an exposure request to a surface page: id is the relay identifier that the reply names, and surface and method name the request (docs/spec/exposure.md#relay).

host.trace.exposure.reply.description: The host received an exposure reply: id is the relay identifier that the reply names, and from is the surface that sent it, or main for the main page.

host.trace.exposure.unmatched.description: An exposure reply matched no waiting request, and the host refused it: held says where the relay keeps the id, as other-target (a request of another document waits under it), expired, ended, or none (the relay holds no request under it).

host.call.peer-lost.description: A call that a view had open when its view process ended was ended by the host with the reason process-ended: plugin and command name the call (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces).

host.trace.view.presentation-abandoned.description: The presentation wait of a view ended without its presentation: surface names the view and reason is the end, one of process-ended, hidden or unresponsive (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces).

host.trace.view.process-request.description: The host created the web view of a view surface, so its WebContent process is requested (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces).

host.trace.view.process-ready.description: The first ready message of a view arrived after the host created it, so its page runtime started (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces).

host.trace.view.responsive.description: The WebContent process of a view answered its responsiveness check again, so the host sent the view-responsiveness notice with responsive true to the main page of the window (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces).

host.trace.view.unresponsive.description: The WebContent process of a view stopped answering its responsiveness check, so the host sent the view-responsiveness notice with responsive false to the main page of the window (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces).

host.trace.plugin-host.process-request.description: The host created the plugin host web view of the plugin in the window, so its WebContent process is requested (docs/spec/plugin-host.md).

host.trace.plugin-host.process-ready.description: The first ready message of the plugin host page arrived after the host created its web view in the window, so its page runtime started (docs/spec/plugin-host.md#channel).

host.trace.modal.stale-ready.description: A ready request of a modal document named a modal that is not open, so the request changed nothing and was answered ok: modal is the id and instance the number of the request (docs/spec/host-contract.md#contract-cases).

host.trace.status.notify.description: The decision of a host.window notification of a window: decision is sent when the value was sent to the watching connections, unchanged when it equals the value sent last, and unwatched when no connection watches host.window of the window (docs/spec/host-contract.md#contract-cases).

host.trace.sidecar.ready.description: The first message line that a sidecar sent after its spawn by the host: sidecar is the name, pid the process and ms the time in milliseconds from the spawn to that line; it is written once for each spawn (docs/spec/host-contract.md#contract-cases).

host.trace.<event>.description: The performance trace of the host, while it is on.

host.sampler.<event>.description: The sampler of the host, while the trace is on. The memory event `host.sampler.memory` is one reading every five seconds: role is host (rss_host_kb), a registered process role with name, page (the page web content process of the window `window`) or document (the web content process of the document web view `surface` of the window `window`). Each process reading holds pid, rss_kb and footprint_kb; a reading that cannot obtain a size holds error instead of the sizes, and a window whose facts cannot be read holds role, window and error.

host.buffer.dropped.description: A bounded buffer of the host refused a message because it was full; `buffer` names it, `count` is the number of messages (1 for each refusal), `bytes` their size and `reason` the bound that was reached. Not a queue of events, whose loss is `log.dropped`.

page.log.dropped.description: The page queue was full or reached its byte bound and refused events; the page stores the count and the bytes in front of the events that follow.

page.log.clock.description: The round trip in microseconds of the clock request that anchors the clock of the page to the clocks of the host and the resolution in microseconds of the clock of the page; a time of the page differs from the clock of the host by at most half of the round trip plus the resolution. The first batch of a page holds them.

page.log.gated.description: The number of events of the class and the level that the gate of the page refused since the earlier report.

page.start.description: A document of the main page started; a reload starts a new document with a new clock.

page.call.description: A host call of a page; `error` names a refused call.

host.endpoint.call.description: A method that a client of the endpoint called; `args` is the params as received (`null` when absent) cut to 1024 bytes, `error` is the code and the message that the client received.

host.binding.call.description: A host call that the main page or a document of a surface sent; `name` is the snake case name of the call, `args` is the JSON array of the arguments in call order cut to 1024 bytes, `error` is the text that the page received or `the call ended without a result`.

page.command.description: A command request that the page answered; `error` names a failed command.

page.background.session.description: A decision of the background session of a tab: open and reopen send the declared operation, skip sends nothing for a tab whose surface is mounted, stop ends the session of a tab that is shown or whose surface mounted. surface is mounted or absent.

page.plugin.operation.description: The page started an install, update, remove, enable or disable of a plugin; its host call carries the same cids.

page.project.operation.description: The page started the open or the removal of a project; its host calls carry the same cids.

page.tab.state.stored.description: The tab state store wrote the entry of a tab, its state, mark and label included; bytes is the size of the written store.

page.tab.state.orphan.description: The reconciliation at load removed the entry of a tab that no layout of projects.json holds.

page.tab.session.stored.description: Core wrote the session history of the document regions of a tab to tab-sessions/<tab>.json; bytes is the size of the written file.

page.tab.session.dropped.description: The session history of a document region exceeded 1 MiB decoded and was not stored; bytes is its decoded size.

page.tab.session.orphan.description: The reconciliation at load removed the session file of a tab that no layout of projects.json holds.

page.tab.keep.changed.description: core.tab.keep set or cleared the mark kept of a tab.

page.tab.unloaded.description: The memory saver unloaded a hidden tab after host.place replied; trigger is delay, pressure or command.

page.tab.restored.description: The memory saver restored an unloaded tab that was shown; history is false when no session history was captured.

page.tab.restore.failed.description: The restore of a shown unloaded tab failed, or a document region refused its session history at that restore or at the first show of the tab after a restart; the error display of the page shows it.

page.tab.unload.failed.description: An unload attempt ended because a read of the document regions of the tab failed; the tab stays loaded and the error display of the page shows it.

page.tab.unload.skipped.description: A pressure report found no candidate, or an unload attempt ended because a protection appeared or the tab was shown; seq is the number of the last pressure report, 0 before the first.

page.view.call.description: The workbench received a call request of a view (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces, view call). A call with this record and no page.view.reply of the same plugin, surface and id has not replied.

page.view.reply.description: The workbench sent the reply of a view call to the view; outcome is result or error, and the reply carries the same id as its page.view.call.

page.view.call.cancel.description: Closing the surface canceled the reply of this received view call; no reply was sent to the ended view.

page.view.event.cancel.description: Closing the surface canceled delivery of this view event after the host refused it because the view had ended.

page.input.shortcut.failed.description: A command that a view ran through runtime.command failed, and the command is the command of a workbench shortcut row (packages/workbench/shortcuts.json); the view ran it for its own forwarded key.

page.window.operation.description: The page started a new window, the close of its window, or the report that the window stays open; its host call carries the same cids.

page.overlay.dropped.description: The page dropped the reply of a modal that the host relayed: `id` names the modal of the reply, `key` its control, and `shown` the id of the modal that the page shows or the empty text when it shows none or has no receiver for it.

page.settings.change.description: A change of the settings by the command or the surface named in actor; keys lists the changed keys and never their values; the write to the host carries the same cids.

page.update.operation.description: The page started the application update to the version; its stage and apply calls carry the same cids.

host.input.relay.description: The host relayed an image region event that carries correlation identifiers to the page; `name` is the region and `type` the type of the event.

host.sidecar.request.description: The host queued a page request that continues inputs for a sidecar; the request line carries the same identifiers, and `bytes` is the size of the body.

host.sidecar.write_wait.description: A line for a sidecar waited a second or more in the write queue of the host, or its write took 10 ms or more.

host.sidecar.reply.description: A message of a sidecar that names the correlation identifiers of a request or states an error, or the failure of a sidecar that ends the requests it did not answer.

host.window.event.description: A window event that the host registered.

host.overlay.dropped.description: The host dropped the reply of a modal document because that modal is not the open one: `id` and `instance` name the modal of the reply, `key` its control, and `open` the id of the open modal or the empty text when none is open. A closing modal still sends its last state report, so a drop is not an error.

host.app.event.description: An application event that the host registered.

host.sidecar.start.description: A sidecar process of standard input and output started.

host.sidecar.connect.description: The host connected to a persistent service.

host.sidecar.disconnect.description: The connection to a persistent service ended. end is how it ended without a protocol violation: eof when the service closed its output, unfinished line when the output ended in a line without a line break, read error with the reader's text, or violation when the service violated the protocol. waiting is the number of requests that waited for the connection when it ended. The exit status of the service is not recorded: the host does not own the process of a persistent service.

host.sidecar.restart-limit.description: A sidecar of either transport failed for the fourth time within 300 seconds, so the host stopped its restarts (docs/spec/sidecars.md#failure).

host.plugin-host.restart.description: The page process of the plugin host of the plugin failed below the restart limit, so the host created the plugin host again; attempt counts the restarts since the last reset (docs/spec/plugin-host.md#restarts).

host.plugin-host.restart-limit.description: The plugin host of the plugin failed for the fourth time within 300 seconds over every window, so the host stopped its restarts and closed it in every window (docs/spec/plugin-host.md#restarts).

host.trace.plugin-host.restart-reset.description: The person opened a surface of a plugin whose plugin host was stopped at its restart limit: the host cleared the failure record and created the plugin host again (docs/spec/plugin-host.md#restarts).

host.trace.sidecar.restart-reset.description: A surface that did not send to a sidecar stopped at its restart limit was opened, or the person enabled a plugin that lists it: the host cleared the failure record, and the next request starts the sidecar. The surface field names the opened surface and the plugin field names the enabled plugin (docs/spec/sidecars.md#failure).

host.project.removal_allowed.description: A window ended while it was asked whether a project may be removed, so the removal is allowed.

host.workspace.settings.description: A settings file changed; scope is common or the project id, set and removed are the sorted keys joined by commas.

host.notification.event.description: The notification center reported a state or a notice that was posted or activated.

host.test.start.description: A window check marked the start of a test; run is the identifier of the test run.

host.test.end.description: A window check marked the end of a test; result is pass, fail or skip.

host.panic.description: A goroutine or a thread of the host panicked; name is the name that the entrance gave it, text is the panic value (the Rust host prefixes `<file>:<line>: `), and the process ends after the event is stored.

host.run.unrecorded-end.description: A process.lock that was not locked when this run started was left by an earlier run that ended without removing it, and this run took it over. boot and pid are the boot identifier and the process identifier of that run when the file is the current form, and null otherwise; previous holds the content of the file, cut to 256 bytes, when the file is not the current form.

host.view.killed.description: The host ended a view that it observes (kill, close or crash); plugin and surface name the view, and unsent is true because the records of the view that were not yet sent to the writer may be lost, which the event states and no count gives. The writer stores it through its own path, so it passes every gate.

host.view.call.description: The host forwarded a call request of a view to the main page of its window (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#view-surfaces, view call). A call with this record and no host.view.reply of the same plugin, surface and id has not been answered by the host.

host.view.reply.description: The host forwarded the reply of a view call to the view; outcome is result or error, and the id is the id of the call.

host.stall.description: The heartbeat of the main thread of the host was late_ms milliseconds late, 1 s or more: the main thread ran nothing else in that time. watch_late_ms is the lateness of the watch's own wake beyond its 250 ms beat: at least half of late_ms means the process was not scheduled, and less than half means the main thread was blocked.

host.stall.sampled.description: The file in the logs folder with the stacks of the threads of the host during a stall of its main thread; error states why the file was not written.

host.stall.resumed.description: The main thread of the host ran again after a stall of stalled_ms milliseconds.

host.stall.dump.description: A host that did not answer has its threads sampled into the file at path.

host.crash.found.description: The system wrote a crash report of an earlier run of the application; the start of the host announces it once.

host.log.index_rebuilt.description: The index of an event file was built from the whole file, because it did not exist or was not the index of that file.

host.relaunch.start.description: The host started the detached command that starts the application again after the process ended (diagnostics.host.relaunch).

host.update.start.description: The host started the detached command that replaces the application bundle.

native.app.activated.description: The application became active: `previous_pid` and `previous_bundle` name the application that the workspace activated last before it, which was frontmost when this one became active, or 0 and the empty text before the workspace activated another application.

native.document.backforward_cleared.description: A document region cleared its back-forward cache, so going back loads the page again. reason is hidden when the region stayed hidden for the hidden clear delay and pressure when the system reported memory pressure.

native.memory.pressure.description: The memory pressure source of the process reported a change of level. level is normal, warn or critical and seq numbers the reports of the process from 1; each host relays the report to the pages as the page event memory-pressure.

native.window.key.description: A window became the key window.

native.window.main.description: A window became the main window.

native.window.occlusion.description: The occlusion state of a window changed.

native.window.first_responder.description: The first responder of a window changed, seen at its next update.

native.input.key_down.description: A key reached an image region. The native layer assigns the correlation identifier of the input here; `before` and `after` hold the state of the input document.

native.input.callback.description: A callback of the input method or a step of the region that it causes (`setMarkedText`, `insertText`, `unmarkText`, `doCommandBySelector`, `commitThrough`, `reportPreedit`, `commitPending`, `clearDocument`, `becomeFirstResponder`, `resignFirstResponder`), with its arguments next to `call` and the state of the input document before and after. It takes the identifier of the input that caused it.

native.input.report.description: A report of a region to the page, as the JSON text that was sent; `dropped` is true when the region was closed and the report was not sent. The sent report carries the identifier as its member `cids`.

native.input.source_changed.description: The selected keyboard input source changed.

native.input.query.description: A query of the input method that an image region answered; `answer` holds the answer.

native.observe.registered.description: An observer, monitor, key-value observer, run loop observer, dispatch source, Apple event handler or delegate was registered through the native entrance; `registrations` counts the registrations of the source.

native.observe.failed.description: The native entrance refused a registration or a delivery that names no registered source.

native.observe.delivered.description: One delivery of a registration of the mode `record`; `count` is the exact number of deliveries of the source so far.

native.observe.counted.description: The deliveries of a registration of the mode `count` since the earlier summary (at most one per second), their total and the microseconds between the summaries.

native.log.gated.description: The number of events of the class and the level that the gate of the native library refused since the earlier report.

native.process.exit_timeout.description: A process did not end within the time that the caller waited for it.

native.webview.process_ended.description: The WebContent process of an app DOM webview ended. reason is the name of the WebKit termination reason (exceeded-memory, exceeded-cpu, requested-by-client, crash, exceeded-shared-process-crash-limit, or unknown-<n> for a value that WebKit defines later) and code is its number.

native.webview.input.description: An input registration of a web view changed phase: registered when the registration is attached to the web view, ended when the registration is unregistered (it is still alive), and released when its last reference is dropped. phase is the name of the phase, view is the address of the web view that identifies its records, and count is the number of live input registrations after the phase.
